rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should test a balanced multimodal configuration with strong components (scgpt RNA encoder, ImageNet ViT-L image encoder, transformer aggregation, and concat fusion) to establish a baseline. This clarifies the effectiveness of key design choices (multimodal vs. single-modal, encoder architectures, aggregation methods) and reduces uncertainty about promising directions.

The existing evidence shows config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) achieves 0.507 accuracy. This experiment tests changing fusion from concat to weighted in the same setup, exploring if weighted fusion improves performance. It's a focused exploitation of the multimodal/multiprofile direction with minimal changes, clarifying the impact of fusion method.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scgpt RNA encoder, weighted fusion, and transformer aggregation (config_026) achieve the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from imagenet_vit_l to resnet50 (a stronger baseline for image tasks) further improves performance while maintaining the effective fusion and aggregation strategies. It balances exploitation of the current best setup with exploration of a key component (image encoder) that could yield significant gains.

The existing evidence shows that weighted fusion with multimodal settings (config_026) outperforms other configurations. This experiment tests whether changing the aggregation method from transformer to avgpool while keeping RNA encoder (scgpt), image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), and weighted fusion could improve accuracy. It clarifies the impact of aggregation methods on performance, balancing exploitation of the current best setup with exploration of alternative components.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and concat fusion, which explores the impact of changing the image encoder and aggregation method while retaining the high-performing RNA encoder. This balances exploitation of the current best RNA encoder with exploration of potential improvements via different image encoders and aggregation strategies.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scgpt RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (e.g., config_016) achieve the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests a different RNA encoder (scvi_n200) and image encoder (resnet50) with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion, which could clarify if these components or aggregation methods further improve performance. It balances exploration of key design choices while building on the promising multimodal multiprofile setup.

Existing evidence shows config_017 (multimodal, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests the same RNA encoder and fusion method but with imagenet_vit_l image encoder, clarifying if image encoder choice impacts performance. It balances exploitation (building on top performer) and exploration (testing critical component variation).

Existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_013) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests a variation with avgpool aggregation to determine if it improves performance, balancing exploration and exploitation of the promising scvi_n200/imagenet_vit_l direction.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 as RNA encoder (e.g., config_017, config_013) achieve high accuracy (up to 0.725). This experiment tests scvi_n200 with resnet50 image encoder and avgpool aggregation, which has not been evaluated yet. It clarifies whether avgpool aggregation (vs. transformer) with resnet50 improves performance, leveraging the strong RNA encoder while exploring a new image encoder-aggregation combination. This balances exploitation of promising components (scvi_n200) with exploration of alternative design choices.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (e.g., config_013 with 0.725 accuracy) perform best. This experiment tests aggregation=None and fusion=weighted, which could clarify if omitting aggregation improves performance. It directly builds on the top-performing components while exploring a new design choice (aggregation method) with high potential impact.
